title: Finite scalar mates as maps of coherent coefficient systems
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\pi,v$, and a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $A_n=R/\pi^n$, $B_n=S/\pi^nS=S/v^{en}$, where $e$ is the ramification index. Work on fixed small pro-etale skeletons with completed coefficient sheaves $\widehat R_W,\widehat S_W$ and bounded derived-complete constructible categories $\mathcal C_R(W),\mathcal C_S(W)$ for $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Let $T_W=-\widehat\otimes_R^L S$ be the prescribed strict-tower scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $T_{W,n}=-\otimes_{A_n}^LB_n$. Use the constructible adjunctions $F_R=Rf_{!,R}\dashv G_R=Rf_R^!$ and $F_S\dashv G_S$, with units $\eta_R,\eta_S$ and counits $\varepsilon_R,\varepsilon_S$, as realized by [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. Fix one compactification of $f$ for these functors [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $\alpha:T_YF_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_ST_X$ be the compact-support scalar comparison obtained by total inverse limit of the finite-free comparisons $\alpha_n:T_{Y,n}F_{A_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{B_n}T_{X,n}$: on a basis of the finite free $R$-module $S$ they are finite-sum distributivity. Use the canonical completed-scalar comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] when commuting $T$ with total limit. For $M\in\mathcal C_R(Y)$, put $M_n=M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}(A_n)_Y$. The finite exceptional comparison $b_{n,M_n}:T_{X,n}G_{A_n}M_n\to G_{B_n}T_{Y,n}M_n$ is the transpose of
$$F_{B_n}T_{X,n}G_{A_n}M_n\xrightarrow{\alpha_{n,G_{A_n}M_n}^{-1}}T_{Y,n}F_{A_n}G_{A_n}M_n\xrightarrow{T_{Y,n}\varepsilon_{A_n,M_n}}T_{Y,n}M_n.$$
In the simultaneous derived coefficient-system realizations of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], these finite transposes define a natural morphism of normalized derived $B_n$-coefficient systems, with quotient transitions those of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] and the finite-free coefficient squares of [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. This is the coherent transpose on those system realizations, rather than a lift chosen only by its finite evaluations. Its total derived inverse limit, under the specified comparisons of source with $T_XG_RM$ and target with $G_ST_YM$, is the $F_S\dashv G_S$ transpose of
$$F_ST_XG_RM\xrightarrow{\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}}T_YF_RG_RM\xrightarrow{T_Y\varepsilon_{R,M}}T_YM.$$
The equality is an equality of the natural integral maps obtained from the specified system realizations.

proof.text:
Choose the fixed compactification $f=pj$ from the definition of the finite compact-support functors. For $A_n=R/\pi^n$ and $B_n=S/\pi^nS=S/v^{en}$, the finite-free extension statement gives that $B_n$ is finite free over $A_n$, and its projection comparison is a natural isomorphism. Applying it to $p$, and using $Rf_{!,A_n}=Rp_{*,A_n}j_!$, gives a finite natural isomorphism
\[
\alpha_n:T_{Y,n}F_{A_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{B_n}T_{X,n}.
\]
On a basis of $S$ this is the finite-sum distributivity map, and its definition as the canonical projection comparison makes it independent of the basis. The coherent system realization is specified in Step 3.

source.place: finite scalar extension paragraph: compact support commutes with finite free coefficient tensor

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], the reductions of $M$ have a uniform finite Tor interval, so each $M_n$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_n)$. For $M_n\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_n)$, use the finite enriched adjunction to define $b_{n,M_n}$ as the transpose of
\[
F_{B_n}T_{X,n}G_{A_n}M_n\xrightarrow{\alpha_{n,G_{A_n}M_n}^{-1}}T_{Y,n}F_{A_n}G_{A_n}M_n\xrightarrow{T_{Y,n}\varepsilon_{A_n,M_n}}T_{Y,n}M_n.
\]
The realization theorem supplies the actual enriched evaluation and transpose maps on simultaneous resolutions, so this is an actual morphism with the displayed source and target. Its evaluation is the stated finite mate, including its unit and counit identities.

source.place: finite scalar extension paragraph: transpose the compact-support comparison through the finite adjunction

proof.text:
Use the simultaneous enhanced section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], with their strict realizations in the derived semilinear-system categories. Derived coefficient extension gives the cofinal system functor
\[
\mathsf T_W^{(e)}(N)_n=N_n\otimes_{A_n}^{L}B_n.
\]
Its transitions are tensor reassociation followed by the transition of $N$; normalization follows from derived tensor associativity. That lemma explicitly supplies simultaneous section models for the direct-image coefficient projection comparison and its composite with open extension. Use this specified construction, applied to the fixed compactification, for $\alpha^{\mathrm{sys}}$; its evaluations are the canonical $\alpha_n$ of Step 1. These evaluations are isomorphisms by [lem-coef-finite-free-extension], so the system comparison is an isomorphism by evaluation conservativity. Coefficient compatibility is therefore realized before total limit, rather than inferred by lifting a commuting diagram of homotopy classes. Restriction to the retained $S$-levels $en$ retains this construction and its quotient transitions.

source.place: finite scalar extension paragraph: coefficient compatibility of the finite comparisons

proof.text:
Transpose $\alpha^{\mathrm{sys}}$ in the tensor-Hom adjunction of the simultaneous system realizations. Explicitly, apply the system-level tensor-Hom evaluation to
\[
\mathsf F_S\mathsf T_X^{(e)}\mathsf E_RN\xrightarrow{(\alpha^{\mathrm{sys}})^{-1}}\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}\mathsf F_R\mathsf E_RN\xrightarrow{\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}\varepsilon_R}\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}N.
\]
The evaluation calculus says that tensor-Hom evaluations and transpositions are maps and identities of derived coefficient systems induced by simultaneous resolutions. Hence this transpose is a natural system morphism $b^{\mathrm{sys}}:\mathsf T_X^{(e)}\mathsf E_R\Rightarrow\mathsf E_S\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}$, rather than a map reconstructed from its evaluations. Evaluating its $n$-component gives exactly $b_{n,M_n}$ from Step 2, while the quotient maps commute by Step 3 and the quotient cocycle for the finite exceptional maps.

proof.text: The $S$-system in Steps 3--4 is indexed by $B_n=S/v^{en}$, a cofinal subsystem of the full $S/v^m$-tower. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], every integral constructible input has the required uniform finite-reduction Tor interval; this also applies to $G_RM$, which is integral constructible by [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. The integral compact-support comparison [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison] applies to the fixed compactification and the derived-complete constructible finite-Tor input: it constructs the integral comparison from compatible finite tensor comparisons on the cofinal strict reduction towers, with those maps fixed before derived limits and with the ordinary tensor presentations identified by the completed-scalar comparison. Thus the total limit of the retained $B_n$-system is canonically the total limit over all $m$, with the specified projections. The exceptional system uses the same coherent finite reductions fixed by [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint], so its target is identified with the corresponding integral exceptional object under these projections.

proof.text: Take the total derived inverse limit of the actual system morphism $b^{\mathrm{sys}}$. The completed finite-free scalar comparison identifies the limit of $N_n\otimes_{A_n}^{L}B_n$ with the prescribed strict-tower scalar extension $N\widehat\otimes_R^{L}S$, naturally and by an isomorphism for derived-complete $N$. The scalar-extension comparison [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension] is exact and preserves the integral bounded constructible categories; since $G_RM$ and $M$ are in the corresponding $R$-categories, this puts $T_XG_RM$ and $T_YM$ in the $S$-categories before $F_S$ and $G_S$ are applied. Together with Step 5 and the coherent realization of integral exceptional pullback, this identifies the limit source with $T_XG_RM$ and the limit target with $G_ST_YM$. The limit of $\alpha^{\mathrm{sys}}$ is the specified $\alpha:T_YF_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_ST_X$. Therefore the limit of $b^{\mathrm{sys}}$ is a well-defined natural integral map $b:T_XG_RM\to G_ST_YM$ constructed before any projection is considered.

source.place: finite scalar extension paragraph: passage from finite comparisons to integral compact support and exceptional pullback

proof.text:
Before taking the limit, the system-level transpose identity says that the adjunct of $b^{\mathrm{sys}}$ is exactly
\[
\mathsf F_S\mathsf T_X^{(e)}\mathsf E_RM\xrightarrow{(\alpha^{\mathrm{sys}})^{-1}}\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}\mathsf F_R\mathsf E_RM\xrightarrow{\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}\varepsilon_R}\mathsf T_Y^{(e)}M.
\]
The coherent integral realization in [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] fixes the exceptional system, its units and counits, before applying total inverse limit. Apply the normalized reconstruction adjunction calculus [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus] to these normalized systems: it states that the descended integral adjunction is $\mathcal L\mathcal F\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L\mathcal E\mathcal R$ and that the adjunct of a descended map is the total limit of its system adjunct. Thus the integral adjunction is the total limit of the system adjunction, and two integral maps are equal after comparing their adjuncts as system maps via the unit/counit identities. Applying the limit functor to the displayed identity and using the completed-scalar comparison transports it to the adjunct of $b$, namely
\[
F_ST_XG_RM\xrightarrow{\alpha_{G_RM}^{-1}}T_YF_RG_RM\xrightarrow{T_Y\varepsilon_{R,M}}T_YM.
\]
This proves the required mate equality as an equality of integral maps; it is not inferred from equality of their finite projections.

source.place: finite scalar extension paragraph: transposing through the integral adjunction identifies the mate

proof.text: All constructions in Steps 1--4 are natural in $M$ and in morphisms of coefficient systems: the finite-sum comparison, quotient transitions, tensor-Hom transpose and their unit/counit equations are natural chain maps on the simultaneous models. Total inverse limit, the cofinal compact-support comparison and the completed-scalar comparison are natural as well. Hence the limit map $b$ is natural, and the equality in Step 7 is an equality of the specified natural integral maps. The constructions remain valid for $E=L$, $f=\mathrm{id}$, $M=0$, $n=1$, and empty schemes (the corresponding systems and limits are zero or identity systems).
